facts.text: The simulation node declares the string parameters simulator and robot and the boolean parameter unlock_base.
The launch file defaults simulator to pybullet and unlock_base to False; robot is a declared launch argument with no default.
The node selects Go2Configuration when robot is go2 and G1Configuration when it is g1.
UnitreeSimulation creates a publisher for the robot's LowState type on /lowstate with queue size 10 and a nav_msgs/Odometry publisher on /odometry/filtered.
The node imports Empty from std_msgs.msg and Odometry from nav_msgs.msg for its ROS 2 interface.
The robots configuration imports LowState and LowCmd from unitree_go.msg.
Go2Configuration returns LowStateGo2 from lowstate_msgs_type and LowCmdGo2 from lowcmd_msgs_type.
The node creates a subscription for the robot's LowCmd type on /lowcmd with queue size 10 and callback receive_cmd_cb, and initialises last_cmd_msg to a default-constructed LowCmd.
When unlock_base is false, the node subscribes std_msgs/Empty on /unlock_base with queue size 1 and its callback calls unlock_base().
The node subscribes std_msgs/Empty on /reset with queue size 1 and its callback calls reset().
The node creates a timer with the robot's high_level_period.
Go2Configuration returns high_level_period 1.0/500.0 and low_level_sub_step 12.
n_dof is len(joint_names).
Go2Configuration lists the 12 joint names in FR, FL, RR, RL order with three joints per leg.
The timer callback reads q, dq, tau, kp and kd from the first n_dof motor_cmd entries of last_cmd_msg.
For each high-level step the node computes tau_cmd = tau_des - kp*(q_current - q_des) - kd*(v_current - v_des) and calls simulator.step once per low-level sub-step.
The callback publishes motor_state mode=1, q and dq for every Go2 joint.
Go2Configuration.foot_force_to_val returns 14.2 + 0.562 * force.
When the robot has feet sensors, the callback publishes int(foot_force_to_val(force)) for every contact force in LowState.foot_force.

The callback rearranges the base quaternion from xyzw to wxyz, publishes gyroscope as the local angular velocity and accelerometer as local linear acceleration plus the rotated gravity vector 9.81; a comment on the gravity rotation says this seems wrong.
The callback fills Odometry with frame odom and child frame base, pose x/y/z and the xyzw quaternion and twist linear/angular values from the simulator state.
The receive callback only assigns the message to last_cmd_msg.
reset() calls simulator.reset() and, when unlock_base_default is true, also calls simulator.unlock_base().
unlock_base() logs and calls simulator.unlock_base().
The abstract wrapper documents unlock_base as releasing a base that was spawned fixed in the world and reset as resetting the simulation and re-locking the base.
The node's constructor creates publishers, subscriptions and a timer only; it creates no ROS service server or action server.
reset() does not assign last_cmd_msg.

BulletWrapper.reset moves the base to q_start and every joint whose id passes 'if id:' (a joint at index 0 does not) to its q_start value, sets zero-force velocity control on the joints and creates a fixed constraint that locks the base when none exists.
The README describes the package as a ROS 2 simulation of the Unitree Go2 that mimics its ROS 2 API by replicating the most-used topics.
package.xml describes the package as a basic simulator wrapper that mimics the real Go2 ROS 2 control API.

determinism.notes: Event-driven rosbridge fake with no physics step, timer pacing, contact model or state-hash replay; placeholder LowState and Odometry samples

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free rosbridge contract stand-in, not a recording of captured traffic: it runs no pybullet or Simple physics, timer, contacts, foot sensors or wall-clock loop

the /lowstate and /odometry/filtered values are placeholders; the first sample of a subscription echoes the last LowCmd q/dq, and later samples are a placeholder stream (joint dq 0.4 until kp, kd and tau are zero, then 0) spaced on the wall clock, not pybullet and not the 500 Hz timer
the motor_state q and dq entries are a placeholder echo of the last published LowCmd, used only as a contract effect; they are not pybullet-measured joint state
the fake models one /lowcmd message as the node stores it, but it does not reproduce the 500 Hz timer, the 12 low-level sub-steps per callback, the torque formula or the base lock
/reset and /unlock_base are recorded only; the fake has no pybullet simulator to reset or unlock and no base constraint
the G1 variant is out of scope: it uses unitree_hg messages, 29 joints and a 1 kHz period, which a single static rosbridge declaration on /lowcmd cannot also carry
the fake returns exactly 12 motor entries and four foot-force entries for Go2; it does not carry the other LowState fields of the real unitree_go message

the node has no stop service or action; the e-stop is a sensed-confirmation stop (SAFE-049, simulated only) that publishes twenty zero MotorCmd entries on /lowcmd and is achieved only when twelve /lowstate joint velocities (arrival freshness, min_interval_ms 1, publisher at simulation_node.py:56) and the stamped /odometry/filtered twist (:57, :139) hold for three samples spanning 4 ms within 1500 ms, which is three samples at the 500 Hz timer; thresholds are operator_required placeholders in fixtures/estop-confirmation.json

the Go2 timer period is 1/500 s (robots_configuration.py:169-171). Three samples span 4 ms (min_span_ms 4). A slower timer still confirms while the gap stays under max_gap_ms 500. A stream closer than min_interval_ms 1 restarts the arrival count. Raising min_span_ms above 4 without a matching slower period fails closed. A replay spaced at or above min_interval_ms is not distinguished from live samples (the same residual as a fresh topic read-back)
/reset and /unlock_base are not the stop: reset() does not assign last_cmd_msg (simulation_node.py:180-183), so those publications stay ordinary commands
the default launch sets unlock_base false (launch/launch_sim.launch.py:9-19), so the base can sit still while the legs move; the predicate therefore includes the twelve joint velocities
the stop request sends 20 MotorCmd entries because that is the requested wire shape; this clone only shows n_dof 12, and the unitree_go array length is outside the clone

a live run requires a colcon/ament workspace with rclpy, unitree_ros2 messages, unitree_description, numpy, scipy and pybullet, plus the operator's rosbridge; none of them is installed, started or validated here

the node mimics the real Go2 ROS 2 API on the same absolute topics (/lowcmd, /lowstate; README.md:3, package.xml:6), so on a graph that also carries a real Go2's unitree_ros2 bridge a /lowcmd publication of this package would reach the real robot; nothing in the package can tell the two apart

the unitree_go LowCmd and LowState definitions are outside the clone: the node indexes motor_cmd and motor_state of default-constructed messages (simulation_node.py:62, 81-85, 98-108), so both are pre-sized arrays, and unitree_ros2 declares them with 20 entries; rosbridge may then refuse this package's 12-entry motor_cmd publication, and a real LowState carries more motor_state entries than the 12 the node fills (the read no longer fixes their count)
the fake's Odometry is a placeholder in the ROS 2 shape; its LowState carries only mode, q and dq per motor entry, not the other MotorState fields of the real message
